name: media-tabs
purpose: A band split in two: a stack of claims on one side, one piece of media on the other, and only the selected claim's media on screen. The selection moves on hover, on click, and on a timer, so the band reads on its own and still answers a reader who takes it over. Its height is its own — each row carries a height the component sets from `size`, and the media column is exactly as tall as the stack — so the band never inherits a height from the section it lands in. `position` decides where the tabs sit: `left` or `right` stack them beside the media, `top` or `bottom` lay them in one row, each with its own title, description and progress, with the one piece of media running the full width on the other side.
useWhen: For a run of peer claims that share one picture frame — three ways a platform is fast, four things a product does.
When each claim needs a sentence of its own, not a bullet: the copy is the content and the media illustrates it.
As a product-page band that rewards watching but does not require it.
avoidWhen: For one claim beside one picture → use `media-split`.
For switching a page's content between peer views the reader navigates → use `tabs`, which is a real ARIA tab set.
related: media-split` — one claim, one picture, no selection.
illustration` — the official scene a tab's `media` slot usually holds.

frame-box` — the registration frame the band is built from: every tab is its own frame and the media column is one more, each with all four corner marks. Every tab flushes its top rule and the media column its top and left rules, so the band draws no top rule of its own: the rule above it (a section title's, or the page frame's) is the only one, and a shared edge is one hairline.
section-title` — the heading above the band; this component carries no title of its own.
bestPractices: Write the tabs as peers. A reader arrives mid-rotation, so no row may depend on the row above it.
Keep a tab's title to one line and its description to two. The row has a fixed height, and copy that overruns it pushes the media column taller than the design.
Give every tab a medium: the frame holds one at a time and cross-fades within it, so a tab with nothing to show reads as a broken rotation, not as a quiet one.
Use scenes of the same shape. The frame does not resize between tabs.
Pick `size` from the copy, not from the section: `medium` holds a title and two lines, `large` a title and four. In a row of tabs, `small` drops each title one step so five claims fit.

Leave `autoplay` on for a band a reader is expected to watch. It pauses under the pointer or keyboard focus, restarts its count on a click (and keeps running under the pointer that clicked), and never starts under reduced motion.

props.name: items
props.doc: The tabs, in order, at most three when `position` is `left` or `right` and five when it is `top` or `bottom`; each item is `{ title, description, src, alt }`. Items past the limit are not rendered.

props.name: position
props.doc: Which side of the media the tabs sit on. Below the `lg` breakpoint every position stacks, with the active tab's media inside its row.

props.name: size
props.doc: Height each row is held to beside the media, as a multiple of the band's own padding step; in a row of tabs, `small` sets the title one step down.

props.name: selectOn
props.doc: What moves the selection as the reader points at a row. A click always selects, on either setting.

props.name: autoplay
props.doc: Advances to the next tab on a timer; pauses under the pointer or keyboard focus, restarts its count on a click, and never runs under reduced motion.

props.name: autoplayInterval
props.doc: Milliseconds each tab is held before the band advances.

props.name: showProgress
props.doc: Advances a hairline along the active row's bottom edge while the timer runs.

props.name: texture
props.doc: Texture the media column is grounded with; `none` leaves it bare.

props.name: textureSize
props.doc: Pitch of the ground's tiling — how far apart its cells sit.

props.name: textureFade
props.doc: How the ground fades out before the column's edges.

events.name: tab-change
events.notes: The selection moved; `index` is the tab now shown. Fires on a reader's hover or click, not on an autoplay tick.

slots.name: media
slots.scope: { item: MediaTabsItem, index: number, active: boolean }
slots.notes: The tab's media; replaces the image built from `item.src`.

examples.name: Default
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import Illustration from '@aziontech/webkit/illustration'
  import MediaTabs from '@aziontech/webkit/media-tabs'

  const scenes = ['ai-applications', 'live-debugging', 'deploy-secure-mcp-server']

  const items = [
    {
      title: 'Run AI models close to users',
      description:
        'Execute models on the Azion Web Platform across hundreds of locations to deliver real-time responses with median latency under 30 ms.'
    },
    {
      title: 'Watch every inference as it happens',
      description:
        'Tokens, latency and error rate per model arrive as the traffic does, with no agent to install and no sampling window to wait out.'
    },
    {
      title: 'Ship a model the way you ship code',
      description:
        'One command puts a new revision in every location at once, and the one before it stays a rollback away.'
    }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <MediaTabs :items="items">
    <template #media="{ index }">
      <Illustration :name="scenes[index]" />
    </template>
  </MediaTabs>
</template>
